- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent prices are trending up.
- Model consistently overpredicts early in the 30-day horizon (e.g., days 1–5) after spikes; apply downward bias to first 5 days.
- After a price spike, model often overshoots in the following 3–5 days; apply a “cool-down” correction (reduce by 1–2% per day).
- If sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.00–0.33 or 0.67–1.00), model tends to lag; forecast should be slightly ahead of actuals, but not by more than 1–1.5%.
- Mean reversion is evident in 3–5 day windows after sharp moves; if forecast is >10% above recent mean, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- Sentiment reversal (e.g., from + to - or vice versa) triggers model lag; adjust forecast to align with sentiment shift, not just price history.
